newsitem.title: USA: Dlr mixed at U.S. close amid interest rate jitters.
newsitem.headline: Dlr mixed at U.S. close amid interest rate jitters.

text.p: The dollar closed mixed in the U.S., rescued by profit-taking from an overnight mark rally and buffeted by mounting fears Wednesday's Tankan report will show strong economic growth in Japan, dealers said.
The dollar fell overnight against the mark and Swiss franc, but recovered in New York trading on profit-taking after a break of technical support at 1.4750 marks, dealers said.
"Basically we hit some stops, but failed to take it any lower. We saw some covering of those short positions and consolidated higher," said Seth Garrett, chief currency dealer at CS First Boston.
Against the yen, the dollar stayed in a narrow range, surrendering modest overnight gains in U.S. trade as investors pondered the Tankan economic report from Japan due Wednesday.
Many dealers expect the quarterly report to show enough strength to build a case for higher Japanese interest rates.
"The Tankan is supposed to favor a recovery for Japan," said Greg Perman, chief dealer at Credit Commericale de France. "But I think people will sell the dollar tomorrow either way."
The dollar closed higher at 1.4781/89 marks Tuesday, up from 1.4759/62 at the open, but fell to 107.65/75 yen from 107.84/94. The dollar rose to 1.1930/40 Swiss francs from 1.1902/09.
Investors had expected the dollar to rally after the Bundesbank aggressively lowered Germany's repo rate to 3.0 percent from 3.3 percent last Thursday.
But the dollar has failed to rally and many market players have begun to price in eventual German monetary tightening, dealers said.
"People are still trying to decide whether the Bundesbank has made its final rate cut," said Seth Garrett, chief currency dealer at CS First Boston.

In addition, some players have been disappointed by the dollar's inability to overtake relatively minor technical resistance at 1.48 marks and 108 yen in recent sessions and are looking for reasons to sell.
"The longs are not getting enough bang for their buck," said Greg Perman, chief dealer at Credit Commerciale de France.
Like Monday's session, Tuesday saw light volume with little force behind any of the day's price moves, dealers said.
"We saw reasonable amounts of trading going through early, but there was little follow-through," added Garrett.

In late New York trading the dollar got a minor boost from a Reuters Fiancial Television interview with U.S. Treasury Secretary Rubin, who reiterated the administration's commitment to a strong dollar, dealers said.
"There was an extremely minute blip when he said that, but it's not really news. We know they don't want the dollar collapsing against the yen," Garrett said.
Shortly thereafter the dollar fell by a similar amount when the Treasury announced the results of its latest auction of two-year notes, which some analysts deemed disappointing.
"The auction didn't go great and there's a fear that Japanese investors own a little too much of our Treasuries," Perman said.
Dealers expected a more active session on Wednesday after the Tankan's release.
"People are waiting for that report to come out," Perman said. "It's been so dead in the last 48 hours it's not funny."

In other trading, the British pound fell to $1.5542/49 from $1.5579/85 at the open. The dollar fell to Canadian $1.3680/85 from C$1.3690/95. The Australian dollar slipped to $0.7880/85 from $0.7890/95.
--Chris Stetkiewicz, 212-859-1664
